name: Concentrix Corporation
business: Designs and runs outsourced customer experience operations, AI and automation, and digital services for enterprise clients in technology, retail, telecom, financial services and healthcare.

events.what: No CEO or CFO change in window: own 8-K Item 5.02 query (2024-07-01 to 2026-10-02) returned only director resignations (Olivier Duha 2025-06-03; GBL designee Bilge Ogut 2026-04-29 after GBL cut its stake below the nomination threshold), plan amendments, and EVP Customer Success Cormac Twomey stepping down 2026-12-31
Tuck-in acquisition of CastleHill Managed Risk Solutions, funding in fiscal Q4 2026 (small, no Item 1.01/2.01 8-K)

next_event.source: Caldwell, Q2 2026 call, document_id 196282: margin expansion magnitude to be discussed 'at the end of this fiscal year' (fiscal year ends November 2026, so likely the Q4 FY2026 call; date not announced)

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Company frames non-GAAP operating margin; only near-term guides exist (Q4 FY2026 about 12.9%, up 20 bps YoY; Q3 FY2026 actual 12.6% operating and 14.8% adjusted EBITDA, both up 30 bps). No multi-year level, annual rate or savings target. Baba FY labels match company fiscal years (November FYE).

statements.quote: All of that would lead to believe that there's still margin expansion capabilities. The magnitude of that, I think we'll talk about at the end of this fiscal year.
statements.speaker: Chris Caldwell

statements.quote: The midpoint of our profitability expectations for the fourth quarter implies a non-GAAP operating income margin of approximately 12.9%, up 20 basis points from the fourth quarter last year. This is consistent with our expectation all year that we would generate year-over-year margin expansion in the second half of the fiscal year.
statements.speaker: Andre Valentine

statements.quote: Our non-GAAP operating income margin was 12.6%, and our adjusted EBITDA margin was 14.8%, with both measures up 30 basis points from the third quarter last year.
statements.speaker: Andre Valentine

street.gap_assumption: No margin target stated, so no gap. Consensus already models about 64 bps of EBITDA margin expansion FY2026 to FY2027 then flat. Only 3 EBITDA brokers.

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [FQ2 2026, FQ3 2026]. FQ2 from consensus actual EBITDA/revenue; FQ3 (reported 2026-09-29, not yet in VA actuals) is the CFO's stated +30 bps adjusted EBITDA margin (doc 225528). LTM 14.3% is FQ3'25 to FQ2'26 VA actuals. Revenue now declining (Q4 guide -3% to -5% constant currency); $1.05B goodwill impairment in FQ3.

disqualifier_reason: No catalyst in the 18-month window and none pending: CEO Caldwell in seat since December 2020 (DEF 14A, doc 461) and CFO Valentine unchanged; own 8-K Item 5.02 query shows only director resignations and an EVP departure, and Item 1.01/2.01 returned nothing; only acquisition is the small CastleHill tuck-in.
verdict: Not the archetype: deeply cheap (3.6x EBITDA, down 74%) with stabilized estimates, but no leadership change or transformational deal, and margin talk is qualitative with the magnitude deferred to the fiscal year-end call.
open_questions: What margin magnitude does Caldwell put on the 'margin expansion capabilities' at the Q4 FY2026 call (likely January 2027)?
Does AI-driven service compression (revenue guided -3% to -5% constant currency in Q4) structurally lift margin or just shrink the base?
Does GBL's exit from the board and stake reduction change governance or invite an activist?
